<!--
documentmode: thesis is APA manuscript mode with the Temple University
Graduate School's front matter, and the title page is the first of it.

The title is set in capitals in an inverted pyramid: the first line longest,
each line after it shorter. The lines are worked out in lua rather than left
to each format, because a .docx can measure nothing while it is being
written, so all four are given the same ones and the page has the same shape
in all four.

Under the title, three centred blocks -- what the work is, what degree it
answers to, who wrote it -- each set off by a rule 5.5 inches wide, and the
examining committee flush left at the foot.

The page carries no number and no running head. After it come the copyright
page, the abstract and the dedication, numbered in lower-case roman, and then
the body, which begins again at 1 in arabic.

The examining committee begins where the rules above it begin rather than out
at the margin, and the abstract begins at the margin with no first line
indented.

The table of contents lists the front matter in capitals, then the chapters
under a label reading CHAPTER with their arabic numbers, then the back
matter: the references, and the appendices lettered in the order they are
mentioned. It lists neither the copyright page nor itself, and it lists as many levels
of heading as toc-depth asks for --- one here, which is the chapters and
nothing under them, against the three quarto counts by default.

In the body every level-one heading is in capitals, and over each chapter
stands the word CHAPTER and its number, set like the heading under it. Only a
chapter gets one: the references and the appendices have a part of their own
to play. The CHAPTER lines are not in the contents, which lists a chapter by
its own name, and each chapter begins a page of its own.
-->
